## Overview

This week starts the R part of the course, which runs through week 15.
R is a great tool for
statistical analysis and visualization of any kind of data,
and probably the best environment for the "downstream" analysis of omics data.
Over these four weeks, we'll build up to analyzing the gene counts
for the RNA-seq data set that you ran the nf-core _rnaseq_ pipeline on in week 11.

This week, we will cover the basics of the R language
and the Positron IDE.
We will also start writing our R code in Quarto documents:
Markdown files with executable code chunks.

At the start of Monday's class, we'll install Positron and set up its connection to OSC
by following the [Positron setup page](./w12a_positron-setup.qmd).

There is only one class this week, on Monday,
because of Veterans Day on Wednesday.

## Learning goals

Some of the things you will learn this week:

#### [Positron setup](./w12a_positron-setup.qmd)

-   Installing Positron and connecting it to OSC

#### [Introduction to R, Positron, and Quarto](./w12b_r-basics.qmd)

-   The Positron layout and the functions of its different regions and panes
-   The basics of interacting with R, using R as a calculator
-   How to create R objects (variables) by assigning values to them
-   How to call R functions
-   How to install and load R packages
-   How to get help in R
-   Why you should open a folder in Positron rather than changing R's working directory
-   How to write, run, and render R code in a Quarto document
